mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average, the real interest rate is expected to decline, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the low-rate period, or FEDFUNDS re-enters higher rates without a subsequent return boost.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in hourly wage growth (implied via UNRATE) signals weakening labor market strength, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate slower corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 150,000 and UNRATE < 6% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar labor weakening events, or wage growth recovers without a sustained return drag.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above trend for two consecutive months suggests strengthening economic demand, which is expected to boost corporate earnings and drive a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains below trend for the next 8 weeks, or 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three months suggests the Fed may pause rate hikes, lowering risk aversion and increasing equity valuations, which should produce a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for the horizon, or the S&P 500 shows no mean reversion to trend.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of residential mortgage applications (not directly available in the catalog) proxy is inferred from HOUST (household utilization) rising above 110%, it suggests excess demand for credit, interpreted as a risk of financial stress and a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such episodes, or HOUST reverts without adverse market reaction.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in unemployment (PAYEMS) followed by a sustained decline in job openings (not directly observable here) is expected to reduce market optimism and produce a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return, even if the spike is transient.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative in >80% of such events, or job market recovers without a return drag.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales momentum (implied by GDPC1) above 2% quarterly growth is interpreted as resilient consumer demand, which should drive a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns fail to outperform a 1% risk-free rate benchmark during the high-GDPC1-growth period.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for 4 consecutive months, in the absence of other monetary signals, is interpreted as a softening demand environment that reduces equity risk premia and supports a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the low-CPIAUCSL period, or other strong demand indicators appear.
